about: I’m a senior AI workflow engineer with nine years of experience across AI systems, SaaS automation, data pipelines, APIs, and enterprise platforms. Most recently at OpenTeams, I built production workflows that route requests, draft CRM updates, and give revenue and support teams a cleaner view of what needs a decision.

I came up through software engineering. I started on platform tools and integration services at IBM in Tulsa, then spent three years at SumatoSoft rebuilding customer workflow services, API connectors, and the observability around them. That path left me with a habit I still use: treat an automation like any other production dependency — owned, measured, and safe to change.

These days most of my time goes to the less visible parts of AI operations: intake rules, human review, audit trails, retries, and the handoff between operators and software. I like sitting with the people who do the work, then shipping something they can trust on a busy week.

expertiseLead: The tools and practices I use most, grouped by the work they support.
principlesLead: Five habits I bring to an automation project.

principles.title: Start from the handoff.
principles.body: The useful question is where work stalls between people and tools. A model is only worth adding after that path is clear.

principles.title: Put a name on every step.
principles.body: Routing, approval, and exception paths need an owner. If nobody is accountable for a step, it will come back as rework.

principles.title: Keep a person in the loop where judgment matters.
principles.body: Drafts, suggestions, and triage are good uses of a model. Decisions that carry risk should stay reviewable.

principles.title: Make failure visible.
principles.body: Retries, alerts, and an audit record matter more than a happy-path demo. Operators should see what stalled and why.

principles.title: Leave the next change easier.
principles.body: Connectors, contracts, and runbooks are part of the system. The workflow should still be understandable after the first team moves on.
